_comment: Wiring Sentinel allowlist + declared prerequisites (seed-antigoodhart-wiring-2026-06-01, E2). dynamicEntrypoints suppress un-called-export false positives for capabilities invoked across boundaries the packages/selfheal/src reference graph cannot see (sibling packages, maintenance scripts under packages/selfheal/scripts/, the runtime skill copy, MCP/agent dispatch, and the test suite). This is a CURATED list: every entry was confirmed to have at least one real consumer outside src/. Genuinely zero-consumer exports are intentionally NOT listed so the sentinel reports them (report-and-escalate, never auto-delete).
_crossProcessExports_comment: Env var names SET in src/ (process.env.X = …) that are deliberately consumed by an out-of-process reader the reference graph cannot see (a spawned child / sibling process). The cross-process analogue of dynamicEntrypoints: a write with no in-source read is normally the 'env vars die at process boundaries' defect (unread_env) — list a name here ONLY when an external consumer genuinely exists. Empty today: the one src/ env write (CRYSTALLIZE_APPROVAL_SECRET in cli/crystallize.ts) is read in-process, so it is not flagged and needs no allowlisting.
_sentinelHandoffs_comment: Declared file-sentinel handoffs (cross-process state passed via a file). Each must have BOTH a writer (writeFileSync/appendFileSync/…) and a reader (readFileSync/existsSync/…) in src/, matched by pathFragment against fs-call string literals (robust to join()/computed paths). A one-ended handoff is half_wired_sentinel. Declaration-driven like dataPrerequisites/triggerBindings, so it never produces inferred false positives. Empty today: selfheal/src has no in-package file-sentinel handoffs.
